Subject: Post-demo recap + focused Qs on geo/retention (Medicora)

Hi Lena / Michael —

Thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our end and three focused questions so we can assemble a short, tailored security / architecture note for your SRE and legal teams.

High-level recap:
- You liked the EU-first proposal (customer data residency in Frankfurt).
- Two modes of interest: strict EU-only for PII workloads, and cross-region warm-standby for inferencing resilience for non-PII traffic.
- Next step: short technical note + evidence files for procurement/security.

Questions for clarification (so we don't make assumptions):
1) EU-only PII scope — do you require that all request/response payloads containing any patient-identifiable fields be constrained to EU compute and storage, with no replication outside EU at any time (including backups)?
2) Failover tolerance — for availability, would Medicora accept an architecture where encrypted backups or snapshot replication to a secondary region (outside EU) are allowed but require explicit dual-control (attestation + access controls), or must backups be strictly Geo-locked to EU as well?
3) Audit/logging/window — what's your retention window requirement for request/response logs and audit trails for the initial pilot (options we commonly see are 30/90/365 days)?

Attachments: I attached the one-page matrix we sketched (geo-failover-matrix.xlsx) and the security questionnaire you started (medicora-security-questionnaire.pdf).

Proposed next steps:
- If you confirm Q1–Q3 we will produce a 1–2 page architecture note mapping Redwood features to your controls (pinning, routing policies, KMS/HSM approach, audit export).
- Schedule follow-up demo with Solutions + SRE (30–45 min) next week.

Happy to do a short call to walk through — suggested times are Tue/Wed next week.

Best,

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + focused Qs on geo/retention (Medicora)

Aisha —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers from our security/procurement POV: 

1) EU-only PII: Yes — for any payloads that include patient identifiers (name, national id, contact info, patient id) we require compute and persistent storage to remain within EU boundaries. No replication of PII artifacts outside EU is permitted.

2) Backups / failover: We would accept backups to a secondary region only if those backups are encrypted with customer-managed keys (we control the KMS) and there is a documented incident-only access process (dual-control approval from our SecOps). Preferably, the backups also remain in EU; if a non-EU replication is technically necessary we need explicit written guarantees on access controls and location, and a runbook for how to remove that copy.

3) Retention: For now pilot -> 90 days for logs/audit, but we may move to 365 for full roll-out.

Two additional asks: 
- Can you confirm whether the model KV cache (inference context cache) is considered persistent data that could leave EU when failover occurs? We need clarity on ephemeral vs persisted caches.
- Please provide any SOC2/SRG artifacts and a short note about encryption-in-transit and at-rest for Dedicated/Private modes.

We'll aim to review your architecture note once you send it. We're targeting a vendor decision in January.

Best,
Lena Fischer
Head of IT Security, Medicora Health

Lena / Michael —

Thanks for the quick clarifications — very helpful. Short technical answers to the two detailed items you asked about:

1) KV cache / ephemeral state: Redwood's inference runtime separates short-lived KV cache (per-request/session in memory) from persistent artifacts. By default, KV cache is in-process and ephemeral (not written to persistent storage). For Dedicated and Private deployments we can configure the runtime to ensure caches are memory-resident only on nodes in the pinned region; no cache persistence nor snapshotting occurs unless explicitly enabled.

2) Backups / replication & CMK:
- For Hosted / Dedicated we support region pinning at the tenant level — you can require EU-only compute and storage. For backups, our standard is to store snapshots in the same region; cross-region replication is a configurable opt-in which we only enable with customer agreement.
- We support customer-managed KMS keys (BYOK) so you keep cryptographic control; even if replication occurs the keys remain under your control and Redwood cannot decrypt without your explicit consent.
- Access to backups outside EU would be governed by an incident runbook and require two-person authorization; we can document the process and include it in the contract.

3) Audit & logs: We emit request logs, model invocation metadata (no model weights), and administrative audit trails. Retention is configurable — 30/90/365 days common presets; we can provide a log-export (S3/GCS within EU) for your long-term retention if you prefer to self-manage.

I'll attach a quick one-page mapping (will send as a Drive link) that maps each ask to the specific Redwood control (pinning flag, CMK, audit export, retention TTL). Vivek, please add any infra caveats below.

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference

Great — thanks all for the quick inputs. Lena / Michael, summary + proposed plan: 

Summary of your requirements (confirm if I've missed anything):
- EU-only compute and persistent storage for any PII payloads.
- Backups: preferred EU-only; if non-EU replication required it must use your CMK and require dual-control/incident-only access.
- Pilot retention: 90 days for logs/audit (may expand to 365 later).
- KV cache is acceptable as ephemeral if kept memory-resident in EU nodes; no snapshotting of cache for PII.

1) We'll produce a 1–2 page architecture note that maps each requirement to Redwood controls, include a simple runbook for backup access and CMK usage (target: by 2026-12-08 COB).
